caption: The first onboarding screen of the Reclaim app before any calendar was linked: Connect your calendars, the line Link your calendars so Reclaim can help you find time for what matters most., a Work calendar card with the button Connect with Google, a greyed Personal calendar card with Connect with Google and Connect with Outlook, the hint Don't have a work calendar? Just connect the calendar you use the most. and a Continue button that is greyed out. There is no skip or later option. The logo says reclaim.ai from Dropbox. No account detail is on this screen.

The public pricing page of Reclaim (the header now reads Dropbox Reclaim) with the yearly toggle: the plan cards Lite (Free, Free forever, 5 AI Agents, 1 user team, 1 week scheduling range, 1 Calendar Sync), Starter ($10 per seat/month, 10 AI Agents/seat, up to 10 seats, 8 week scheduling range, 3 Calendar Syncs) and Business ($15 per seat/month, 100 AI Agents/seat, up to 100 seats, 12 week scheduling range, Unlimited Calendar Syncs). The lower part of the cards lies below the visible part. No account detail is on this screen.

The same public pricing page with the Monthly toggle selected: Lite Free, Starter $12 per seat/month and Business $18 per seat/month, with Business marked Most Popular and the same Dropbox Reclaim header. No account detail is on this screen.

The Planner of the Reclaim app on the Lite plan, week of 15 to 21 November: the habit called Test focus block as a solid block on Wednesday 18 from 10 to 11am and as dashed (provisional) blocks on Thursday 19 and Friday 20, with the Reclaim Tasks panel on the right listing four tasks (two onboarding tasks of Reclaim and our two test tasks Review test notes and Draft test report) that have no block in the calendar. The banner at the top offers premium features free for 30 days plus 30% off the first year. The tester had covered the avatar at the top right with black; it stays covered.
